scope: scripts/qualify_drives.py --run-native at bfa633fe (build frozen at artifacts/dv2, --artifacts artifacts/dv3), 28/28 steps: an owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with an added SINAMICS G120C PN (6SL3210-1KE21-3AF1, firmware 4.7.14), whose DriveObject.DriveObjectNumber Startdrive cannot read. drive_observe addresses its one drive object by container index (driveObjectIndex 0, driveId DO@0) with the native error as a warning. drive_parameter_set (p1082[0], System.Single, 1500 to 12.5) prepares by the index handle and refuses a stale expected value (ExpectedValueMismatch), an unknown parameter (ParameterNotFound), the number handle (DriveObjectHandleMismatch) and p0971 (SafetyBoundary); drive_telegram_set (main telegram 1 to 20, 4/4 to 12/4 input/output bytes) prepares by the index handle and refuses a safety telegram (SafetyBoundary) and stale expected telegrams (ExpectedValueMismatch). Each applies with checkpoint, device compile (the PLC station compiled, the drive listed as not compiled) and save, change_status reports the applied stages, drive_observe reads the change back, and the checkpoint restore brings back the original value or telegram rows. After detach and Host close (exit code 0) the owned TIA process exited (279 ms).
limitations: One G120C PN on an owned scratch, not connected to the CPU's IO system; offline engineering values only (no online values, upload, download or RAM-to-ROM).
The drive's telegrams carry no address ranges off the IO system, so the telegram address-shift report and overlap check ran on empty ranges; supplementary and additional telegrams are not exercised.
One floating-point parameter per change; numbered drive objects and drives with several drive objects are not exercised.
The drive object identity is the hardware path, the container's object count, order number, firmware and parameter count; BICO sources on index-addressed drives stay unresolved.
The wrong-handle refusal ran on drive_parameter_set; drive_telegram_set resolves the drive object through the same code.
